findings.where: Hero, the 'Get in touch' button (desktop and phone first screen); the page has no footer
findings.fault: The only contact route is a button that silently opens a mail program (mailto). Its arrow suggests it goes to a contact page. Mark's email address is never shown as text anywhere, and no footer repeats it, so a visitor can't see or copy where the message would go.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer on a locked-down work machine or using webmail. Clicking either does nothing or launches an unconfigured mail client, and with no visible address to copy they have no route to Mark, which is the page's one action.

findings.where: Hero, the line under the heading ('Advice on infrastructure projects and the laws that enable them…')
findings.fault: The first screen says what Mark does but not who he does it for (development banks, agencies, governments) or where he has worked (regions or countries). It only says 'international'. A reader can't tell within 5 seconds whether this advisor has worked for bodies like theirs in their region.
findings.who_objects: The brief's audience, multilateral development bank staff who select consultants by project type and region. 'International' gives them nothing to match against their terms of reference.

findings.where: Hero, 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience'
findings.fault: The credibility claim is a size word, a count of years, rather than a checkable fact such as a named body, role or date. It reads as a boast in the firm voice the client wants to avoid.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader judges relevant experience, not tenure, and discounts headline year counts. Mark's own brief asks for 'confident without big-firm claims, no boasts'.

findings.where: Hero, the space beside and below the 'Get in touch' button
findings.fault: Next to the call to action there's no proof beyond the one World Bank line: no selected work, no body that asked for his advice, no recent talk with its venue. The visitor is asked to write before seeing any evidence of work like theirs.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor from a development agency who needs to know he has done this kind of work for organisations like theirs before they write.

findings.where: Article specimen, the line under the title ('MMM Infra Blog No. 8 · 18 September 2024')
findings.fault: The article page carries no author name or one-line bio. It's credited to 'MMM Infra Blog', so a reader arriving straight from a LinkedIn post meets a firm label instead of the man.
findings.who_objects: A reader who lands on an article from a social post and wants to know who is speaking. It also goes against the brief's 'the individual is the brand' and 'Mark is seen and heard'.

findings.where: Article specimen, the related link 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' with 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF'
findings.fault: The lecture is labelled without the venue or the body that hosted it. The one sign of standing it could give, who asked Mark to speak, is missing.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader, for whom 'invited by X' is the credibility signal. An unnamed lecture says little.
